title: gate misses a command whose first word expands to nothing
detail: When a simple command's leading words expand to empty at runtime, bash runs the next word as the command: `$(:) rm a`, `$(:) 2>&1 rm a`, `$x > f rm a` (x unset) all remove a. Neither v0.238.8 nor the one-bash-lexer reader reads `rm a` there; v0.238.8 read `$(:) >! rm a` only by accident (it took `>!` as a write target). A substitution with no output, or an unset variable, cannot be resolved statically in general; candidate rule: when the command name is an unquoted expansion the gate cannot resolve, also judge the remaining words as a command (over-read, fail-closed). Found by the regression-sentinel's fuzz in fix round 4 of one-bash-lexer.
